changed: Codex review round 6 on H4, three findings fixed with regression tests: guarding hook commands end in || exit 2 (close-check only unattended) so a python3 that cannot start the script denies; tomllib imported lazily so check-scope runs on Python 3.9 and bash-guard fails closed there; compose stop/start/restart/pause/unpause read the compose files and .env the working directory loads (COMPOSE_ variables, include/extends, container names) and ask after cd; a persisted docker context that is not a local socket asks. Live check on Claude Code 2.1.231 after the change.

rulings.ruling: Compose targets are checked by reading container_name lines in the compose files the working directory would load, not by running docker compose config
rulings.cost_if_wrong: a compose file that sets names through anchors or other YAML features the line check misses passes; the sandbox compose file uses plain names

rulings.ruling: A docker context counts as local when its endpoint is a unix or npipe socket
rulings.cost_if_wrong: a unix socket forwarded from a remote host is treated as local (deliberate setup, outside the habitual-command model)

rulings.ruling: Editing .claude/settings.json hook commands to end in || exit 2 hardens fail-closed behaviour; no permission rule changed
rulings.cost_if_wrong: none for status and checkpoint, which keep their non-blocking behaviour
